correctness.rationale: Fixed-point-freeness makes the center trivial, gives free complement orbits on nonidentity kernel elements, and makes each nontrivial complement coset one conjugacy class. The abelian kernel and cyclic complement give the two clique blocks. A mixed pair cannot commute; if it generated a nilpotent subgroup, its coprime Hall factors would commute, contradicting the same fixed-point-free action. Metabelianity makes the solvable graph complete. For the collision family, invariant-line counts in the characteristic derived subgroup distinguish the two groups. The included verifier independently enumerates the two finite examples at p=7 and p=13.

value.rationale: The primary survey explicitly motivates graph-determination questions. The theorem supplies a complete, closed-form description for a natural infinite structural family and shows a specific limitation of all three conjugacy-class graphs: they erase the fixed-point-free module action. The scalar-versus-split family turns that structural blindness into uniform nonisomorphic collisions, so the result is substantially stronger than merely checking disconnectedness or one small example.
